title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
description:
Given the `head` of a singly linked list, remove the `n`-th node from the end of the list (`1`-indexed from the tail) and return the head of the modified list.

If removing that node leaves the list empty, return `null` (`None` in Python). Try to complete this in a single pass using `O(1)` extra space.
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is sz.
hints: Attach a sentinel (dummy) node before `head` so removing the head node (`n == sz`) is handled identically to any other node.
Maintain two pointers `slow` and `fast` starting at the dummy node, and advance `fast` by `n` steps first.
Move both `slow` and `fast` one step at a time until `fast.next` is null; then `slow` is immediately before the target node.

examples.explanation: The 2nd node from the end is 4; removing it produces [1, 2, 3, 5].
Removing the only node leaves an empty list (null).
The 1st node from the end is 2; removing it leaves [1].
